look_here_first: TANGLEHEAD: native warm-season perennial tuft whose tightly clustered fertile florets bear extraordinarily LONG TWISTED or bent dark awns, which eventually TANGLE together as seedheads mature. Look for the paired sessile and pedicelled spikelets under 10× and the pale hairy raceme around them. A fresh un-tangled head can still be diagnostic from its long awns.

crew_field_check: Compare Bothriochloa, Schizachyrium, and Dichanthium with their much smaller/shorter or differently clustered racemes and awns. The dramatic long contorted individual awns are a strong clue; whole rooted clump and paired spikelets confirm.
Confirm true collar, ripe spikelets and habit from the same source-identified individual.
